name: al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula
callout_language: Yemeni Arabic; tribal hosts' local dialects in Shabwa, Abyan and al-Bayda.

doctrine.summary: AQAP formed in 2009 from the merger of al-Qaeda's Saudi and Yemeni branches and is regarded as one of the network's most capable affiliates. It briefly held territory in southern Yemen (Abyan in 2011-2012, Mukalla in 2015-2016) before being pushed back to desert and mountain areas of Abyan, Shabwa, al-Bayda, Marib and Hadramawt. Leader since March 2024: Saad bin Atef al-Awlaki, after Khalid Batarfi's death. The US National Counterterrorism Center (2026) estimates 2,000-3,000 fighters. Its main enemies on the ground are the UAE-backed southern forces (Southern Transitional Council units, Security Belt, Shabwa Defence Forces) and the Houthis. Since 2022 it has run a long campaign of IEDs, raids on outposts and small quadcopter drone attacks in Abyan and Shabwa. In the game AQAP is an early-game desert-raid enemy: small fast-moving cells in pickups and on motorbikes, IED hazards on desert roads, night raids on checkpoints.
doctrine.fireteam: Raiding groups of 5-15 in pickups, built from cells of 3-5; local tribal hosts provide guides. In game: 2-4 battle-buddy pairs.
tactics: Night raids on isolated checkpoints and outposts from wadis, then withdrawal into the desert
IED hazards on desert and mountain roads, telegraphed for the player to spot and clear
Quadcopter drone munition drops on outposts as an AI hazard ability
Ambush from wadis and ridgelines on supply convoys
Retreat into tribal villages, keeping the casualty rule active

notes: AQAP is a UN-listed and US-designated terrorist organisation and an affiliate of the al-Qaeda core (relation al_qaeda 90). It has attempted external attacks (2009 underwear bomb plot, 2010 cargo plot) and claimed the 2015 Charlie Hebdo attack. Leader: Saad bin Atef al-Awlaki since March 2024; in 2025 he called for attacks on senior US officials. NCTC (May 2026): about 2,000-3,000 fighters, mainly in southern and central Yemen. Reported 2026 activity includes clashes in Wadi Omran (Mudiyah, Abyan) in February 2026. The Houthis are an enemy (they fight in al-Bayda), although the UN Panel of Experts reported some tactical coordination in 2024; that value is kept negative. Game framing: early-game raid enemy in yemen_red_sea; contracts against AQAP come from Saudi, Emirati or Yemeni-government-linked clients.
proposed: relations.houthis (enemy with reported limited coordination; low-confidence magnitude)
